summary: The root WDY primarily means to pay blood-money or compensation for a life. It also refers to the act of giving or presenting something, often as a gift or offering.

headwords.gloss: He gave the bloodwit to the heir; next of kin, of the slain person

parts.t: He gave the bloodwit to the heir,
next of kin, of the slain person.

headwords.def: وَدَى القَتِيلَ He gave the bloodwit to the heir, or next of kin, of the slain person. (Msb.)
وَادَاهُ inf. n. مُوَادَاةٌ , He took [ from him ] the دِيَة . (TA.) See 3 in art. عدو .

headwords.gloss: It destroyed him; it removed him; took him away

parts.t: (M, K:) said of death [&c.]. (T, M, K.) See an ex. in art.

headwords.def: أَوْدَى بِهِ It destroyed him; (T;) it removed him, or took him away: (M, K:) said of death [&c.]. (T, M, K.) See an ex. in art. بلو , conj. 8, and another voce أَزْلَمُ . أَوْدَى : see a verse cited voce قَلَبَةٌ . أَوْدَى العَيْرُ إِلّا ضَرِطًا : see ضَرَطَ .

headwords.gloss: Bloodwit; a fine for bloodshed; homicide; Fines for wounds
headwords.def: دِيَةٌ Bloodwit; a fine for bloodshed, i. e., homicide; consisting of a hundred camels. دِيَاتُ جِرَاحَاتٍ [ Fines for wounds ]. (S, M, TA, &c., in art. شنق .)

headwords.gloss: Small; shoots; offsets, cut off from palm-trees and planted

parts.t: offsets, cut off from palm-trees and planted:

headwords.def: وَدِىٌّ Small فَسِيل , q. v.; (S, Msb, K;) shoots, or offsets, cut off from palm-trees and planted: (Mgh:) young palm-trees. (TA.)

parts.t: through which a torrent runs forth
]: (Msb:) for which reason it is thus called. (M, Mgh, TA.)
in one of the senses explained in art.

headwords.def: وَادٍ [ A valley; a water-course, or torrent-bed: and sometimes a river; ] a space intervening, (M, Msb, K,) i. e. any such space, (M, Msb,) between mountains or hills; (M, Msb, K;) through which a torrent runs forth [ occasionally or constantly ]: (Msb:) for which reason it is thus called. (M, Mgh, TA.) حَلَّ بِوَادِيهِ i. q. بَاعَِ عَلَى بَيْعِهِ in one of the senses explained in art. بيع ; i. e., (tropical:) He superseded him, &c.
